questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.85]\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,4.4);\draw[->] (0,0)--(9,0);\draw[thick] plot[smooth,tension=0.6] coordinates {(0.3,0.1)(0.9,1.6)(1.7,3.4)(2.5,2.7)(3.3,1.95)(4.3,1.3)(5.3,0.85)(6.3,0.5)(7.2,0.25)(8.1,0.08)};\node[below] at (4.05,0) {Reaction time};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which description best fits this distribution?

options.why: Names the skew from the peak on the left instead of the longer tail on the right.
Ignores that the right-hand tail is much longer than the left-hand tail.
Counts two peaks even though the curve has only one.

questions.solution_text: The longer tail extends to the right, so the distribution is positively skewed.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.6]\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,11);\draw[->] (0,0)--(6,0);\draw (0.5,0) rectangle (1.5,1);\draw (1.5,0) rectangle (2.5,2);\draw (2.5,0) rectangle (3.5,4);\draw (3.5,0) rectangle (4.5,10);\draw (4.5,0) rectangle (5.5,6);\node[below] at (3,0) {Time used};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which description best fits the distribution of quiz finishing times?

options.why: Names the skew from the tall columns on the right instead of the longer tail on the left.
Treats the unequal tails on either side of the peak as mirror images.
Treats the two tallest neighbouring columns as two separate peaks.

questions.solution_text: The columns taper towards the left of the peak, giving a longer left-hand tail. The distribution is negatively skewed.

questions.question_text: A student scored $7, 4, 7, 4, 7, 3, 7, 2$ in eight tests. Which measure of centre would the student prefer to tell their parents to make their performance appear best?

options.why: Chooses the middle score calculation without comparing it with the higher mode.
Chooses the average of all scores without comparing it with the higher mode.

questions.solution_text: The mean is $41 \div 8 = 5.125$, the median is $(4 + 7) \div 2 = 5.5$ and the mode is $7$. The mode is highest, so it makes the performance appear best.

options.why: Chooses a position below the rising side of the curve rather than directly below its peak.
Chooses the middle marked position rather than directly below the highest point of the curve.

questions.solution_text:
The mode is the most common time, so it sits at the peak of the curve.
The peak is at the right of the three lines, where the curve is highest.
The rightmost line, $R$.

questions.question_text: The delays of ten trains, in whole minutes, were $0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 28$. Which measure best supports an argument that passengers experience substantial delays?

options.why: Chooses the middle delay, which does not reflect the size of the severe delay of $28$ minutes.
Chooses the most frequent delay, which emphasises on-time arrivals rather than substantial delays.

questions.solution_text: The mean is $40 \div 10 = 4$ minutes. It includes the severe delay of $28$ minutes, so it supports this argument better than the median of $1$ minute or the mode of $0$ minutes.

questions.question_text: Consider Dataset 1: $10, 10, 11, 12, 13$ and Dataset 2: $10, 10, 11, 12, 113$. Why is the mean a less suitable measure of centre for Dataset 2?

options.text: The outlier $113$ pulls the mean away from where the other four values lie.

options.why: Confuses the mean with a measure that does not use every value; the mean includes $113$ in the total.

options.text: The repeated value $10$ forces the mean to equal $10$.
options.why: Confuses the mode with the mean; repetition does not force the mean to equal the most frequent value.

options.text: A mean cannot be calculated when there are five values.
options.why: Incorrectly restricts the mean to an even number of values; it can be calculated for either number.

questions.solution_text: Dataset 1 has mean $56 \div 5 = 11.2$. Dataset 2 has mean $156 \div 5 = 31.2$, far above its four ordinary values. The outlier $113$ distorts the mean.

questions.question_text: Eight friends recorded their fun run times, in minutes: $21, 23, 24, 24, 26, 28, 33, 49$. What is the mean finishing time?

options.why: Calculates the median by averaging the fourth and fifth ordered times, $24$ and $26$, instead of calculating the mean.
Reports the mode, the repeated time, instead of calculating the mean.
Omits the longest time, $49$, and divides the remaining total $179$ by $7$, then rounds to two decimal places.

questions.solution_text: The total is $228$ minutes and there are eight friends. The mean is $228 \div 8 = 28.5$ minutes.

questions.question_text: Seven employees each earn $\$34{,}000$ and one employee earns $\$434{,}000$. An advertisement reports the mean salary as $\$84{,}000$. Which statement explains why this is misleading?

options.text: The mean is correct, but the single high salary pulls it above what most employees earn.
The mean must be $\$34{,}000$ because this is the most frequent salary.
options.why: Reports the mode as the mean instead of including every salary in the total.

options.text: The mean must be $\$234{,}000$ because it is halfway between the lowest and highest salaries.
options.why: Averages only the two extreme salaries and ignores their different frequencies.

options.text: Every employee earns $\$84{,}000$ because that is the mean.
options.why: Treats an average as the salary of every individual, although the supplied salaries differ.

questions.solution_text: The mean is $(7 \times 34{,}000 + 434{,}000) \div 8 = 84{,}000$. Seven of the eight employees earn $\$34{,}000$, so the mean does not describe a typical salary. The single high salary pulls it up.

questions.question_text: A student's test scores fall into these categories: 20s: one test; 30s: one; 40s: one; 50s: one; 60s: one; 70s: two; 80s: none; 90s: none. The student reports only that the modal category is the 70s. Why can this be misleading?

options.text: Only two of the seven scores are in the 70s; the other five are lower.
A modal category must contain more than half the scores.
options.why: Confuses being the most frequent category with containing a majority; a mode need not contain more than half.

options.text: The modal category is the 40s because it is the middle listed category with a nonzero frequency.
options.why: Uses category position instead of comparing frequencies to find the modal category.

options.text: There is no modal category because no scores are in the 80s or 90s.
options.why: Treats empty categories as preventing a mode, although the 70s has the highest frequency.

questions.solution_text: The 70s is the modal category because it contains two tests, more than any other category. However, five of the seven scores are below the 70s, so reporting only the modal category makes the overall performance appear stronger than it is.
